intro: You are in the Uşak Archaeology Museum, in Uşak province, opened in 1978. This is the home of the Lydian Hoard from the tumuli of the region, and its emblem is a winged sea-horse brooch that was stolen and recovered years later.
history: The story of this museum is bound up with looting. In the 1960s the Lydian tumuli around Uşak were plundered, and pieces were taken out of the country. They came back in 1993, after a suit brought against the Metropolitan Museum in New York. Ever since, the collection known as the Lydian Hoard has been shown here.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Lydian Hoard and the winged sea-horse brooch, then the finds from the tumuli and the coin collection.
facts: Did you know? The winged sea-horse brooch, the emblem of the collection, was stolen a second time after its return and replaced with a fake; the original was later recovered. And the Lydian Hoard itself was brought back from New York through a lawsuit, years after it had been smuggled out.
outro: This brings our tour of the Uşak Archaeology Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. These treasures travelled far before coming home; help keep them safe. Enjoy your visit.
